(STD-performance-properties-15, should)
  - Why: CSS animations run off the main thread and stay smooth while the browser loads, scripts or paints, while requestAnimationFrame-based animation drops frames (a Vercel dashboard tab animation using Shared Layout Animations dropped frames during page loads until it moved to CSS). WAAPI gives JavaScript control with CSS performance: hardware-accelerated, interruptible, no library.
  - Sources: eks-skills-animate-skill, eks-skills-emil-design-eng-skill, eks-skills-improve-animations-audit, eks-skills-review-animations-skill, eks-skills-review-animations-standards, eks-skills-animate-recipes, eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Treat dropped frames as a regression.** Treat any animation, drag or scroll that drops frames as a failed review, measured against 60fps (120fps on displays that support it, an 8ms frame budget instead of 16ms). Values: baseline `60fps`; high-refresh `120fps`; frame-budget-at-120fps `8ms`. (STD-performance-properties-16)
  - Why: A transition that works but drops frames is a regression, not a pass; not losing frames while dragging is the starting bar, and jittery scroll reads as carelessness. 60fps is the baseline for smooth motion; newer displays run at 120fps.
  - Sources: ek-building-a-drawer-component, eks-skills-review-animations-skill, eks-skills-improve-animations-skill, eks-skills-animation-vocabulary-skill, eks-skills-apple-design-skill, eks-skills-animate-expo-skill.
- **Virtualize long lists and large tables.** Virtualize long lists and large tables so only visible rows render; never render a 1,000+ row list directly. Values: threshold `1,000+ rows`; library `Virtuoso (https://virtuoso.dev); if the project already uses another virtualizer such as react-window, keep it`. (STD-performance-properties-17)
  - Why: A long list that renders everything scrolls slowly; reach for virtualization (Virtuoso) before pagination hacks.
  - Sources: eks-performance-cheatsheet, eks-skills-pick-ui-library-skill.
- **Animate a child to stop hover flicker.** When a hover effect flickers, animate a child element instead of the hovered parent. (STD-performance-properties-24, should)
  - Why: It is the listed fix for hover-caused flicker; the source gives no further reason.
  - Sources: ek-agents-with-taste.
- **Keep per-frame movement small enough.** Keep the per-frame positional change below the perception threshold to avoid strobing. (STD-performance-properties-25, should)
  - Why: Smoothness is about what is in the frames, not just the frame rate.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.

**Accessibility in motion**
- **Ship reduced motion with the animation.** Ship the prefers-reduced-motion variant of every animation that moves something (and, on the web, its hover gating) in the same change as the animation itself, including every prototype variant and every proposed motion recipe, never as a follow-up. Values: css `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`; react `useReducedMotion()`; react-native `useReducedMotion() or reduceMotion: ReduceMotion.System`. (STD-accessibility-motion-01)
  - Why: Animations can cause motion sickness, so reduced motion and hover gating ship with the animation every time; missing reduced-motion handling on movement is flagged on sight.
  - Sources: eks-skills-animate-skill, eks-skills-animate-expo-skill, eks-skills-find-animation-opportunities-skill, eks-skills-prototype-skill, eks-skills-review-animations-skill, eks-skills-emil-design-eng-skill, eks-skills-animation-vocabulary-skill, eks-skills-animate-expo-recipes.
- **Reduced motion is gentler, never zero.** Under reduced motion, remove movement (translation, scale, slides, springs, parallax, elastic and overshoot) and replace it with a short opacity cross-fade (the sources use 200ms, ease) or a static transition, while keeping the opacity and color changes that explain a state change; never remove all animation or feedback. Values: remove `translation, scale, slides, springs, parallax, elastic, overshoot`; keep `opacity and color changes that aid comprehension`; cross-fade `200ms ease`; css-example `.element { animation: fade 0.2s ease; }`; sheet-example `.sheet { transition: opacity 200ms ease; transform: none !important; }`. (STD-accessibility-motion-02)
  - Sets: `raw.reducedMotion` "replace", `motion.duration.reduced-fade` 200ms, `reduced:motion.transition.enter` {"duration": "{motion.duration.reduced-fade}", "delay": {"value": 0, "unit": "ms"}, "timingFunction": [0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1]}, `reduced:motion.transition.exit` {"duration": "{motion.duration.reduced-fade}", "delay": {"value": 0, "unit": "ms"}, "timingFunction": [0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1]}, `reduced:motion.transition.expand` {"duration": "{motion.duration.reduced-fade}", "delay": {"value": 0, "unit": "ms"}, "timingFunction": [0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1]}.
  - Why: Reduced motion means fewer and gentler animations, not zero: a gentler, non-vestibular equivalent that keeps the transitions that aid comprehension, not the removal of feedback.
  - Sources: eks-skills-animate-skill, eks-skills-animate-expo-skill, eks-skills-apple-design-skill, eks-skills-emil-design-eng-skill, eks-skills-improve-animations-audit, eks-skills-review-animations-skill, eks-skills-review-animations-standards, eks-skills-find-animation-opportunities-skill.
- **Branch JS motion values on reduced motion.** In JavaScript-driven motion, read the reduced-motion setting (useReducedMotion(), or Reanimated's reduceMotion: ReduceMotion.System on each animation) and swap movement values for static ones when it is on, for example closedX = reduce ? 0 : '-100%'. Values: react `const reduce = useReducedMotion(); const closedX = reduce ? 0 : '-100%';`; react-native `const reduced = useReducedMotion(); const y = useSharedValue(reduced ? 0 : SHEET_HEIGHT); or withSpring(0, { duration: 300, dampingRatio: 0.8, reduceMotion: ReduceMotion.System })`. (STD-accessibility-motion-03)
  - Why: Reduced motion removes movement and position changes, and the sources' JS route is to read useReducedMotion() and branch the transform values on it.
  - Sources: eks-skills-improve-animations-audit, eks-skills-animate-skill, eks-skills-emil-design-eng-skill, eks-skills-review-animations-standards, eks-skills-animate-expo-skill.
- **Check reduced motion by toggling it.** Put a reduced-motion step in the verification (feel check) of every motion change: toggle prefers-reduced-motion in DevTools' Rendering panel and confirm that movement is dropped while opacity feedback remains. Values: tool `Rendering panel: prefers-reduced-motion`. (STD-accessibility-motion-05)
  - Why: It is a fixed line in the feel check of the implementation-plan template, and the source says the feel check is not optional: motion can be mechanically correct and still feel wrong.
  - Sources: eks-skills-improve-animations-plan-template.
- **Missing reduced motion blocks approval.** In motion reviews and audits, rate movement without prefers-reduced-motion handling as a MEDIUM finding, also report reduced-motion code that removes all feedback, and approve a change only when reduced motion is respected. Values: severity `MEDIUM`. (STD-accessibility-motion-06)
  - Why: The audit rates missing reduced-motion 'noticeably off' (MEDIUM) and hunts both failure modes; the review flags missing reduced-motion handling on movement on sight and lists 'reduced-motion respected' among the Approve criteria.
  - Sources: eks-skills-improve-animations-skill, eks-skills-improve-animations-audit, eks-skills-review-animations-skill.
- **No full-viewport moving backgrounds.** Do not put a moving background behind the full viewport. (STD-accessibility-motion-07, should)
  - Why: The Apple design guidance lists full-viewport moving backgrounds among the motion to avoid in its reduced-motion and accessibility section, whose aim is a gentler, non-vestibular experience.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **No slow looping oscillations near 0.2 Hz.** Do not loop a slow oscillation near 0.2 Hz (about one cycle every 5 seconds). Values: frequency `0.2 Hz`; period `one cycle per 5s`. (STD-accessibility-motion-08, should)
  - Why: The Apple design guidance lists slow looping oscillations near 0.2 Hz among the motion to avoid in its reduced-motion and accessibility section.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Ease theme changes, no brightness jumps.** Ease the switch between dark and light themes instead of letting brightness jump abruptly. (STD-accessibility-motion-09, should)
  - Why: The Apple design guidance lists abrupt brightness jumps among the changes to avoid and says to ease dark/light theme changes.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Soften large surfaces while they move.** Make large moving objects semi-transparent while they travel, and during a large reposition fade big surfaces out and back in once they settle. (STD-accessibility-motion-10, should)
  - Why: Part of the Apple design guidance for reduced motion and accessibility: large moving areas are softened rather than shown travelling at full strength.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Reduced transparency makes surfaces solid.** Handle prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce as its own signal, separate from reduced motion: make translucent surfaces frostier or solid by raising their background opacity and dropping the blur. Values: css `@media (prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce)`; example `.toolbar { background: white; backdrop-filter: none; }`. (STD-accessibility-motion-11)
  - Why: Components respond to three independent signals (reduced motion, reduced transparency, increased contrast), and each one gets its own treatment baked into the component.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Increased contrast gets solid, bordered surfaces.** Handle prefers-contrast: more as its own signal: give surfaces near-solid backgrounds with a defined, contrasting border. Values: css `@media (prefers-contrast: more)`. (STD-accessibility-motion-12)
  - Why: It is one of the three independent signals the source says to bake into components.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Scale layout with the user's text size.** Respect the user's text-size setting (Dynamic Type) by scaling layout with the text; on the web write spacing in rem or em, not fixed px. Values: spacing-units `rem, em (not px)`. (STD-accessibility-motion-13)
  - Why: So a larger font does not break the layout.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Gate hover motion to fine pointers.** Put every :hover animation (and, for mobile web, every :hover style) inside @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine), with both conditions, in the same change as the hover, and leave :active press feedback ungated. Values: css `@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`; tailwind-v4 `the hover: variant already compiles to @media (hover: hover)`; tailwind-v3 `future.hoverOnlyWhenSupported`; press `:active (ungated)`. (STD-accessibility-motion-15)
  - Why: Touch has no hover, so browsers fake one: the first tap applies :hover and leaves it there until the user taps elsewhere. (hover: hover) means the primary input can hover and (pointer: fine) rules out styluses and Android devices that claim hover; :active is a real press on touch, so it needs no gate.
  - Sources: eks-skills-animate-skill, eks-skills-animate-recipes, eks-skills-emil-design-eng-skill, eks-skills-improve-animations-audit, eks-skills-review-animations-skill, eks-skills-review-animations-standards, eks-skills-mobile-native-skill, eks-skills-find-animation-opportunities-skill, eks-readme.
- **Build overlays on accessible primitives.** Build dialogs, drawers, popovers, dropdown menus, selects and tabs on an accessible primitive (base-ui, or Radix such as Radix Dialog and Radix Tabs) that handles focus management, focus trapping and dismissal, and command menus on cmdk; never hand-roll a <div>-based dropdown or dialog with manual focus handling. Values: primitives `base-ui (https://base-ui.com)`; radix `Radix Dialog (Vaul is built on it), Radix Tabs`; command-menu `cmdk`. (STD-accessibility-motion-16)
  - Why: Hand-rolling those is how you end up with a <div> dropdown and no focus management; the primitive makes the component accessible and handles focus trapping and dismissal.
  - Sources: eks-skills-pick-ui-library-skill, eks-skills-animate-skill, ek-building-a-drawer-component, ek-the-magic-of-clip-path.
- **Hide decorative duplicate layers.** When a component stacks a visual-only duplicate of its content (a clip-path overlay copy of tabs or of a button label), mark the duplicate's container aria-hidden and give any buttons inside it tabIndex={-1}. Values: container `aria-hidden`; buttons `tabIndex={-1}`. (STD-accessibility-motion-17, should)
  - Why: The duplicated layer is only visual and the real, focusable controls sit underneath; the source code does this without stating a reason, which is presumably to keep assistive technology and keyboard focus on the real controls [inferred].
  - Sources: ek-the-magic-of-clip-path, ek-building-an-animation-course.
- **Prototype picker: accessible markup and focus.** Build the prototype variant picker with its fixed accessible markup: <nav aria-label="Prototype variants">, aria-hidden="true" on the highlight and divider spans, aria-label="Replay animation (R)" on the icon-only replay button, exactly one item carrying data-active and aria-current="true", a :focus-visible outline of 2px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.4) with outline-offset 2px, and transition: none on the highlight under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce. Values: nav `aria-label="Prototype variants"`; decorative-spans `aria-hidden="true"`; replay `aria-label="Replay animation (R)"`; active-item `data-active + aria-current="true"`; focus-visible `outline: 2px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.4); outline-offset: 2px`; reduced-motion `.proto-picker[data-ready] .proto-picker-highlight { transition: none; }`. (STD-accessibility-motion-18)
  - Why: The picker's appearance is not a design decision; it is the spec, copied verbatim so it always reads as harness chrome.
  - Sources: eks-skills-prototype-picker.
- **Never rely on haptics alone.** Never make a haptic the only feedback for an action; pair it with a visual change that works on its own. (STD-accessibility-motion-20)
  - Why: Haptics are off system-wide for many users and silent on most Android hardware, so the visual has to stand alone.
  - Sources: eks-skills-animate-expo-skill.
- **Keep the toaster labelled and reachable.** Keep Sonner's accessibility defaults on: the toast container's ARIA label ('Notifications', localised through containerAriaLabel), the Alt+T hotkey that focuses the toaster area, and dismissible: true, setting dismissible: false only when the user must not be able to close that toast. Values: containerAriaLabel `Notifications`; hotkey `⌥/alt + T`; dismissible `true`. (STD-accessibility-motion-23, should)
  - Why: Sonner's API gives the toast container an ARIA label and a keyboard shortcut that focuses the toaster area, and with dismissible: false the user cannot dismiss the toast; keeping these defaults as the house default is a reading of the API reference [inferred].
  - Sources: sonner-toast, sonner-toaster, eks-skills-ask-sonner-api, eks-skills-ask-sonner-skill.
- **Never trap the user in an overlay.** Give every screen and overlay a way out: keep drawers dismissible by outside click, Escape and drag by default, and if one must be non-dismissible, give it an explicit close control such as Drawer.Close [inferred]. Values: drawer-default `dismissible: true`; explicit-close `Drawer.Close`. (STD-accessibility-motion-24)
  - Why: Every screen should answer 'How do I get out?'; never trap the user. A non-dismissible Vaul drawer blocks outside click, Escape and drag, and the docs' own demo can then only be closed by refreshing the page; pairing it with Vaul's Close part ('the button that closes the drawer') is our connection [inferred]. (Vaul is good-to-have and unmaintained per its README, recorded in learn/sources.json on 2026-09-24.)
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill, vaul-api, vaul-other.
- **Controlled drawers still react to Escape.** When a Vaul drawer is controlled with the open prop, also pass onOpenChange so the app reacts to Escape and outside clicks. Values: props `open + onOpenChange`. (STD-accessibility-motion-25, should)
  - Why: onOpenChange is called when the open state changes, which the docs call useful for reacting to esc/outside clicks when the drawer is controlled. (Vaul is good-to-have and unmaintained per its README, recorded in learn/sources.json on 2026-09-24.)
  - Sources: vaul-default.
- **Cover the inert page behind a drawer.** While a modal drawer or sheet is open, render its overlay so a layer covers the inert rest of the view. Values: vaul `<Drawer.Overlay />`. (STD-accessibility-motion-26, should)
  - Why: Vaul's Overlay is the layer that covers the inert portion of the view when the drawer is open, and a modal task pairs its surface with a dimming scrim. (Vaul is good-to-have and unmaintained per its README, recorded in learn/sources.json on 2026-09-24.)
  - Sources: vaul-api, eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Never disable pinch zoom.** Never set user-scalable=no or maximum-scale=1 in the viewport meta tag; when the page zooms into an input, fix the input's font size (16px at the minimum) instead. Values: forbidden `user-scalable=no, maximum-scale=1`; input-font-size `16px at the minimum`. (STD-accessibility-motion-27)
  - Why: user-scalable=no and maximum-scale=1 are accessibility failures; the zoom they are used to stop comes from iOS Safari zooming into inputs under 16px, so the font size is the thing to fix.
  - Sources: eks-skills-mobile-native-skill.

**Toasts, drawers and overlays**
- **Mount one Toaster at the root.** Mount exactly one <Toaster /> once, as close to the app root as possible (in Next.js, layout.tsx), and never render it per page, conditionally, or in both a layout and a page. Values: mount `<Toaster />`; next.js `layout.tsx`. (STD-components-toasts-drawers-02)
  - Why: A second mounted Toaster duplicates every toast, and an unmounted one means toasts never appear.
  - Sources: eks-skills-ask-sonner-skill, sonner-getting-started, sonner-home.
- **Keep the Toaster outside stacking contexts.** Mount the Toaster at the document root, outside any dialog or portal container and outside any ancestor with transform, filter or overflow. Values: avoid-ancestors `transform, filter, overflow`. (STD-components-toasts-drawers-03, should)
  - Why: Such an ancestor creates a stacking context, or the overlay out-z-indexes the toaster, so toasts sit behind a modal or get clipped.
  - Sources: eks-skills-ask-sonner-skill.
- **Call toast() only from client code.** Call toast() only from client code (event handlers, effects, callbacks); in a server action, return the result and call toast() in the client code that receives it. (STD-components-toasts-drawers-04)
  - Why: toast() is a plain function that does nothing on the server.
  - Sources: eks-skills-ask-sonner-skill, sonner-getting-started.
- **Fire toasts from handlers or stable ids.** Fire toasts from event handlers; when a toast must fire from an effect, pass a stable id so a repeated call updates the toast instead of duplicating it. Values: effect-fix `stable id`. (STD-components-toasts-drawers-05, should)
  - Why: React StrictMode's dev double-invoke runs effects twice; a stable id makes the second call update rather than duplicate.
  - Sources: eks-skills-ask-sonner-skill.
- **Web toast enter: 400ms ease from below.** On the web, enter a toast from opacity: 0 and transform: translateY(100%) to its settled position with transition: opacity 400ms ease, transform 400ms ease, using @starting-style (or a mounted flag set in useEffect where @starting-style is unavailable). Values: from `opacity: 0; transform: translateY(100%)`; transition `opacity 400ms ease, transform 400ms ease`; entry `@starting-style`; fallback `useEffect(() => { setMounted(true); }, []); <div data-mounted={mounted}>`. (STD-components-toasts-drawers-07, should)
  - Sets: `motion.duration.toast` 400ms, `motion.easing.toast` [0.25, 0.1, 0.25, 1].
  - Why: A toast that suddenly appears feels off; Sonner uses ease rather than ease-out and runs slightly slower than typical UI because its motion is tuned to the component's personality.
  - Sources: ek-building-a-toast-component, ek-you-dont-need-animations, eks-skills-animate-recipes, eks-skills-emil-design-eng-skill, eks-skills-find-animation-opportunities-skill.
- **Stack toasts with lift and depth.** In the collapsed stack, position toasts absolutely, lift each toast behind the front one by the gap times its index, and scale it down by 0.05 per index; apply this only to non-front toasts while the stack is collapsed. Values: scale `scale(calc((-1 * var(--toasts-before) * 0.05) + 1))`; lift `translateY(calc(var(--lift-amount) * var(--toasts-before)))`; examples `Y(0) scale(1); Y(-14px) scale(0.95); Y(-28px) scale(0.9)`; selector `[data-sonner-toast][data-expanded="false"][data-front="false"]`. (STD-components-toasts-drawers-10, should)
  - Why: Absolute positioning simplifies the stacking, and scaling the toasts behind down creates a sense of depth.
  - Sources: ek-building-a-toast-component.
- **Stacked toasts share the front height.** While toasts are stacked, give every toast the height of the toast in front. (STD-components-toasts-drawers-11, should)
  - Why: Toasts with different heights otherwise do not stick out evenly behind the front toast.
  - Sources: ek-building-a-toast-component.
- **Expand the toast stack on hover.** Keep the toast stack collapsed and expand it while the pointer hovers the toast area (expand: false by default); when expanded, offset each toast by its index times the gap plus the heights of the toasts before it, with a gap of 14. Values: expand `false (default)`; offset `heightIndex * GAP + toastsHeightBefore`; gap `14`. (STD-components-toasts-drawers-12, should)
  - Sets: `component.toast.gap` 14px.
  - Why: Stacked mode hides older toasts and hovering reveals them; toasts can differ in height, so each expanded offset adds the real heights above it.
  - Sources: ek-building-a-toast-component, eks-skills-ask-sonner-api, sonner-toaster.
- **Fill gaps between toasts for hover.** Fill the gaps between expanded toasts with an :after pseudo-element so the hover state holds while the pointer crosses a gap. Values: css `:after`. (STD-components-toasts-drawers-13)
  - Why: The gaps belong to no toast, so hovering them would make the toasts lose their hover state (and collapse).
  - Sources: ek-building-a-toast-component, eks-skills-emil-design-eng-skill.
- **Show at most three toasts.** Show at most 3 toasts at once by default (visibleToasts: 3). Values: visibleToasts `3`. (STD-components-toasts-drawers-14, should)
  - Sets: `component.toast.visible` 3.
  - Why: 3 is Sonner's documented default number of visible toasts.
  - Sources: eks-skills-ask-sonner-api, sonner-toaster.
- **Auto-dismiss toasts after 4 seconds, except action toasts.** Auto-close toasts after 4000ms by default, except a toast that carries an action button (Undo, Retry): it stays until the person acts on it or dismisses it (Sonner: duration: Infinity on that toast() call). Values: duration `4000ms`; action-toast `no auto-close: duration: Infinity on that toast() call, until the person acts or dismisses it [inferred]`. (STD-components-toasts-drawers-15, should)
  - Sets: `component.toast.duration` 4000ms.
  - Why: 4000ms is Sonner's default duration: by default the toast disappears after 4 seconds unless you hover over it. A toast with an action is the exception: closing it on a timer puts a time limit on the action, and the accessibility floors outrank every house standard (docs/KNOWLEDGE.md section 2; WCAG 2.2.1 Timing Adjustable), so it persists; this agrees with DC-L08-18 and the Q-form-04 option inline-banner [inferred: no source states the exception].
  - Sources: ek-building-a-toast-component, eks-skills-ask-sonner-api, sonner-toast, sonner-other.
- **Pause the toast timer on hover.** Pause the auto-dismiss timer while the pointer hovers the toasts. (STD-components-toasts-drawers-16, should)
  - Why: The toast disappears after 4 seconds unless you hover over it, so a person reading it keeps it.
  - Sources: ek-building-a-toast-component.
- **Pause toast timers in a hidden tab.** Pause the auto-dismiss timer while the document is hidden (document.hidden and the visibilitychange event). Values: api `document.hidden + visibilitychange`; hook `useIsDocumentHidden`. (STD-components-toasts-drawers-17)
  - Why: A toast fired while the person is on another tab would otherwise time out unseen; an inactive tab should freeze its toasts.
  - Sources: ek-building-a-toast-component, eks-skills-emil-design-eng-skill.
- **Swipe toasts away along their position.** Let people swipe or drag toasts and drawers away, on touch devices and on desktop; for toasts the allowed swipe directions follow the toaster position, and swipeDirections is overridden only when they must differ. Values: swipeDirections `based on position (default)`. (STD-components-toasts-drawers-18, should)
  - Why: People are used to swiping notifications away on their devices, and Sonner derives the swipe directions from the position.
  - Sources: ek-building-a-toast-component, eks-skills-ask-sonner-api, eks-skills-ask-sonner-skill, ek-building-a-drawer-component.
- **Pick the toast call by need.** Pick the toast() call by what the message needs: toast('Title') with { description } for plain messages, toast.success/error/info/warning for status, toast.promise for work tied to one promise, toast.loading plus an update by id when you manage the states yourself, { action } / { cancel } for buttons, and toast.custom for headless JSX. Values: plain `toast('Title', { description })`; status `toast.success / toast.error / toast.info / toast.warning`; promise `toast.promise(promise, { loading, success, error })`; manual-async `toast.loading('…') then toast.success('…', { id })`; action `{ action: { label, onClick } }; event.preventDefault() keeps it open; cancel is the secondary button`; custom-shell `toast(<jsx />)`; headless `toast.custom((t) => <jsx />)`. (STD-components-toasts-drawers-19, should)
  - Why: Typed calls carry the matching icon, the promise toast starts loading and switches to success or error on its own, and the action button closes the toast unless onClick calls event.preventDefault().
  - Sources: eks-skills-ask-sonner-skill, eks-skills-ask-sonner-api, sonner-toast, ek-building-a-toast-component.
- **Promise toasts need a settling promise.** Pass toast.promise a promise, or a function returning one, that actually resolves or rejects. (STD-components-toasts-drawers-20)
  - Why: Otherwise the loading toast waits forever and never closes.
  - Sources: eks-skills-ask-sonner-skill.
- **Update a toast by its id.** To change a toast already on screen, keep the id toast() returns and call toast() (or a typed call such as toast.success) again with that id, passing only the props that change, instead of adding a new toast. Values: example `const id = toast.loading('Uploading…'); toast.success('Uploaded', { id });`. (STD-components-toasts-drawers-21, should)
  - Why: Calling toast() with the same id updates the existing toast, only the props you pass change, and a typed call switches its type.
  - Sources: eks-skills-ask-sonner-skill, sonner-other, eks-skills-ask-sonner-api.
- **Toasts follow the app theme.** In an app with a dark theme, set the Toaster theme to 'system' or pass the theme provider's resolved theme (for example <Toaster theme={resolvedTheme} /> from next-themes). Values: theme `theme="system" or theme={resolvedTheme}`; default `'light'`. (STD-components-toasts-drawers-22)
  - Why: theme defaults to 'light' and does not track the OS, so dark mode is otherwise ignored.
  - Sources: eks-skills-ask-sonner-skill, eks-skills-ask-sonner-api, sonner-toaster.
- **Rich colors and invert from defaults.** Start toast styling from Sonner's defaults: add richColors on the Toaster when success and error must read green and red, and use invert only to flip toasts against the theme. Values: richColors `false (default)`; invert `false (default)`. (STD-components-toasts-drawers-23, should)
  - Why: Success and error toasts are gray by default; richColors and invert are the first rung of the styling ladder.
  - Sources: eks-skills-ask-sonner-skill.
- **Headless toast for the design system.** Build the design system's toast headless with toast.custom() and your own JSX, wrapped in your own toast() function. Climb the styling ladder (defaults, inline style, classNames, headless) only as far as a change needs: the middle rungs suit a few small changes, and a design-system toast should not linger there. Values: headless `toast.custom((t) => <jsx />)`; small-change `toastOptions={{ style: { … } }}`; avoid `unstyled: true (a halfway house; headless gives more control for the same effort)`. (STD-components-toasts-drawers-24, should)
  - Why: Headless keeps Sonner's positioning, stacking and swipe while giving full control, and it is the recommended approach because people usually either use the defaults or go fully custom; styling parts with classes gets messy quickly and is a good compromise only for a few changes.
  - Sources: eks-skills-ask-sonner-skill, sonner-styling.
- **Toast classNames need !important.** When styling toast parts through toastOptions.classNames (toast, title, description, actionButton, cancelButton, closeButton), mark every class !important (Tailwind: the ! prefix) unless the toast is unstyled, and go headless once more than a few classes need it. Values: parts `toast, title, description, actionButton, cancelButton, closeButton`; tailwind `!text-red-900`. (STD-components-toasts-drawers-25)
  - Why: Sonner's injected styles win the cascade, so classes without !important have no effect.
  - Sources: eks-skills-ask-sonner-skill, eks-skills-ask-sonner-api, sonner-styling.
- **Set toast defaults on the Toaster.** Put app-wide toast options in the Toaster's toastOptions and override them per toast() call only where needed. Values: prop `toastOptions`. (STD-components-toasts-drawers-26, should)
  - Why: Options passed to toast() override the same options set on the Toaster.
  - Sources: eks-skills-ask-sonner-api, sonner-toast.
- **Target toasts when several toasters exist.** When more than one Toaster exists, give each an id and pass toasterId in every toast() call. Values: example `<Toaster id="canvas" />; toast('…', { toasterId: 'canvas' })`. (STD-components-toasts-drawers-27)
  - Why: Without toasterId, every toaster renders the toast.
  - Sources: eks-skills-ask-sonner-skill, eks-skills-ask-sonner-api.
- **Handle dismiss and auto-close separately.** Handle user dismissal in onDismiss and timeouts in onAutoClose, and wire both when code must react to every way a toast closes. Values: callbacks `onDismiss, onAutoClose`. (STD-components-toasts-drawers-28, should)
  - Why: onDismiss fires on the close button or a swipe and onAutoClose fires when the toast closes after its duration; there is no single closed callback.
  - Sources: eks-skills-ask-sonner-skill, sonner-other.
- **Toasts default to bottom-right.** Place toasts bottom-right by default, choosing only from top-left, top-center, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-center and bottom-right. Values: default `bottom-right`; positions `top-left, top-center, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-center, bottom-right`. (STD-components-toasts-drawers-29, should)
  - Why: bottom-right is Sonner's documented default and these are its six positions; swipe directions follow the position.
  - Sources: eks-skills-ask-sonner-api, sonner-toaster.
- **Toaster edge offsets: 32px and 16px.** Offset the toaster 32px from the screen edges on desktop and 16px when the screen is narrower than 600px (offset and mobileOffset). Values: offset `32px`; mobileOffset `16px`; mobile-below `600px`. (STD-components-toasts-drawers-30, should)
  - Sets: `component.toast.offset.desktop` 32px, `component.toast.offset.mobile` 16px.
  - Why: These are Sonner's documented default offsets, and mobileOffset applies below a 600px screen width.
  - Sources: sonner-toaster, eks-skills-ask-sonner-skill, eks-skills-ask-sonner-api.
- **Copy Sonner styles into shadow DOM.** When rendering Sonner inside shadow DOM, copy the <style> elements in document.head whose text includes [data-sonner-toaster] into the shadow root. Values: selector `[data-sonner-toaster]`. (STD-components-toasts-drawers-33)
  - Why: Sonner inserts its styles into the document head when the bundle loads, so they are not available inside shadow DOM.
  - Sources: sonner-other, eks-skills-ask-sonner-skill.
- **Import Sonner styles when they are lost.** When toasts render unstyled (Astro, view transitions), import Sonner's stylesheet explicitly in a layout: import 'sonner/dist/styles.css'. Values: import `import 'sonner/dist/styles.css'`. (STD-components-toasts-drawers-34, should)
  - Why: Sonner's injected stylesheet was lost.
  - Sources: sonner-other, eks-skills-ask-sonner-skill.
- **Toast API is a plain function.** Expose the design-system toast as a plain toast() function callable from anywhere, with one <Toaster /> mounted once: no hooks and no React context. Values: api `toast('My toast')`; state `observer pattern: <Toaster /> subscribes, toast() notifies`. (STD-components-toasts-drawers-35, should)
  - Why: No hooks, no context, one insert and a function call is one of the two reasons Sonner succeeded; the less friction to adopt, the more people use it (Sonner avoids context with an observer pattern).
  - Sources: ek-building-a-toast-component, eks-skills-emil-design-eng-skill.
- **Prefer drawers over modals on mobile.** On mobile, present secondary content in a drawer (bottom sheet) rather than a modal. (STD-components-toasts-drawers-37, should)
  - Why: A drawer gives a more native feel on mobile.
  - Sources: ek-building-a-drawer-component.
- **Build drawers on an accessible dialog.** Build drawers on an accessible dialog primitive (Vaul builds on Radix Dialog) with composable, styleable parts: Root, Trigger, Portal, Overlay, Content, Handle, Title, Description and Close. Values: parts `Drawer.Root, Drawer.Trigger, Drawer.Portal, Drawer.Overlay, Drawer.Content, Drawer.Handle, Drawer.Title, Drawer.Description, Drawer.Close`. (STD-components-toasts-drawers-38, should)
  - Why: The dialog primitive makes the drawer accessible and handles focus management, a Radix-like API feels familiar, and not every drawer has to look the same. Vaul itself is unmaintained per its GitHub README (learn/sources.json, checked 2026-09-24); flag that before adding it as a dependency.
  - Sources: ek-building-a-drawer-component, vaul-api.
- **Drawer defaults: modal, bottom, dismissible.** Default drawers to modal, opening from the bottom edge, dismissible (outside click, Escape and drag down), draggable from anywhere rather than only the handle, and portalled with an overlay over the inert rest of the view. Values: modal `true`; direction `bottom`; dismissible `true`; handleOnly `false`; container `document.body`. (STD-components-toasts-drawers-39, should)
  - Why: These are Vaul's Root defaults; dismissible: false blocks all three ways of closing, and the Overlay covers the inert portion of the view. Vaul itself is unmaintained per its GitHub README (learn/sources.json, checked 2026-09-24); flag that before adding it as a dependency.
  - Sources: vaul-api, vaul-other.
- **Drawer curve: cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1).** Animate drawers and sheets that open or close on a timing curve (every web drawer) with the iOS-like drawer curve, defined once as a token: --ease-drawer: cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1) (React Native: EASE_SHEET = Easing.bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1)). Sheets and drawers a finger drives on iOS and Android settle with a spring instead (STD-springs-gestures-08). Values: --ease-drawer `cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1)`; react-native `EASE_SHEET = Easing.bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1)`; native-sheet `spring { duration: 300, dampingRatio: 0.8, velocity }`. (STD-components-toasts-drawers-40)
  - Sets: `motion.easing.drawer` [0.32, 0.72, 0, 1] (STD-enter-exit-origin-41 wins).
  - Why: The curve, from the Ionic Framework, closely matches iOS's sheet; the right easing and duration make a big difference to how the component feels, and built-in CSS easings are too weak.
  - Sources: ek-building-a-drawer-component, eks-skills-animate-skill, eks-skills-emil-design-eng-skill, eks-skills-improve-animations-audit, eks-skills-review-animations-standards, eks-skills-find-animation-opportunities-skill, eks-skills-animate-expo-skill, eks-skills-animate-expo-recipes, eks-skills-animate-recipes.
- **Drag a drawer only from its scroll top.** Let a scrollable drawer be dragged only when its content is scrolled to the top, and block dragging for 100ms after scrolling reaches the top. Values: check `shouldDrag`; drag-lock-after-scroll `100ms`. (STD-components-toasts-drawers-44, should)
  - Sets: `motion.gesture.drag-lock-after-scroll` 100ms.
  - Why: Being scrollable and draggable at once is tricky; this mirrors native iOS drawers, and fast scrolling can overshoot the top into a drag with enough velocity to close the drawer by accident.
  - Sources: ek-building-a-drawer-component.
- **Keep drawer inputs above the keyboard.** When an input inside a drawer opens the on-screen keyboard, stop the browser's scroll-into-view and use the Visual Viewport API to size the drawer to the visual viewport and sit it directly above the keyboard (Vaul: repositionInputs, on by default). Values: listener `window.visualViewport resize`; height ``${visualViewportHeight - OFFSET}px``; bottom ``${Math.max(diffFromInitial, 0)}px`, where diffFromInitial = window.innerHeight - visualViewportHeight`; vaul `repositionInputs: true (default)`. (STD-components-toasts-drawers-45, should)
  - Why: Otherwise the browser scrolls up and pushes the drawer, potentially hiding important content; sitting above the keyboard keeps the drawer fully scrollable, and the author found this works best despite a slight delay. Vaul itself is unmaintained per its GitHub README (learn/sources.json, checked 2026-09-24); flag that before adding it as a dependency.
  - Sources: ek-building-a-drawer-component, vaul-inputs, vaul-api.
- **Fixed-pixel snap points for inputs.** Use a fixed-pixel snap point (rather than a fraction of the viewport) when something such as an input must stick out by the same amount on every device. Values: forms `fraction of the viewport or fixed px`. (STD-components-toasts-drawers-48, should)
  - Why: Fixed values make the content stick out evenly on all devices.
  - Sources: ek-building-a-drawer-component.
- **Safari theme bar must match the overlay.** Sync Safari's theme-color with a drawer overlay only if it stays in step with the overlay: precompute the opaque color the overlay makes over the background, interpolate to it along the drawer's own curve when the drawer opens, pick the color from a linear interpolation by drag progress while dragging, and leave the sync out if it falls out of step. Values: meta `meta[name="theme-color"]`; curve `bezier-easing with the drawer curve`. (STD-components-toasts-drawers-65, should)
  - Why: Linear interpolation will not match a drawer on a custom bezier curve, and the author has not shipped the theme-bar sync in Vaul because it does not match the overlay transition when frames drop.
  - Sources: ek-building-a-drawer-component.
- **Feedback on press, commit on release.** Show press feedback the instant the pointer or finger goes down (:active, or pointerdown / onPressIn when JavaScript is needed) and commit the action on release; never show feedback only on click. Values: css `:active`; js `pointerdown`; react-native `onPressIn (feedback), onPressOut (commit)`. (STD-components-toasts-drawers-72)
  - Why: Waiting for click or touch-up to show anything feels dead and reads as lag even at 0ms, because the finger has already left.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill, eks-skills-animate-expo-skill, eks-skills-mobile-native-skill.
- **Hold to confirm: slow press, fast release.** When a destructive action that a plain click fires too easily uses hold-to-confirm, make the press slow and the release fast: an overlay clipped to inset(0 100% 0 0) fills to inset(0 0 0 0) over 2s linear while pressed and snaps back over 200ms ease-out on release, with scale(0.97) on the button. Values: rest `clip-path: inset(0 100% 0 0)`; pressed `clip-path: inset(0 0 0 0); transition: clip-path 2s linear`; release `transition: clip-path 200ms var(--ease-out)`; button `transform: scale(0.97)`. (STD-components-toasts-drawers-77)
  - Why: Be slow where the person is deciding and snappy where the system responds (symmetric timing on a hold is a review finding); linear is right because the fill is a progress indicator.
  - Sources: eks-skills-animate-recipes, eks-skills-emil-design-eng-skill, eks-skills-animate-skill, eks-skills-review-animations-skill.
- **Dismiss toasts from code by id.** Remove a toast from code with toast.dismiss(id), using the id that toast() returns (or t.id inside toast.custom), and call toast.dismiss() with no id only when every visible toast should go. Values: one `const id = toast('Event has been created'); toast.dismiss(id);`; all `toast.dismiss()`; headless `toast.custom((t) => <jsx />): t gives the id to dismiss`. (STD-components-toasts-drawers-78, should)
  - Why: toast.dismiss(id) is the documented way to remove a toast programmatically; called without an id it dismisses all toasts at once.
  - Sources: sonner-other, eks-skills-ask-sonner-skill, eks-skills-ask-sonner-api.

**Mobile and touch**
- **Detect touch by capability, never by device.** Decide touch behavior with media queries and platform features ((hover), (pointer), env(), dvh), written for touch and mouse at the same time; never branch on user-agent strings or screen width to guess at touch, and never reach for a JavaScript touch-detection hook where a media query does it. Values: capability-features `(hover: hover), (pointer: fine), (pointer: coarse), env(), dvh`; never `user-agent strings, screen width, useIsTouchDevice()`. (STD-mobile-touch-02)
  - Why: Touch and mouse are not exclusive (iPads with trackpads, laptops with touchscreens, phones with a mouse), and almost every mobile fix is one CSS declaration or meta tag, so a useIsTouchDevice() hook to hide hover states is the wrong tool.
  - Sources: eks-skills-mobile-native-skill.
- **Remove the tap highlight flash globally.** Set html { -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent; } once, globally, and give every tappable element its own :active state in the same change. Values: declaration `html { -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent; }`; replacement-feedback `:active on every tappable element`. (STD-mobile-touch-03)
  - Why: The translucent flash iOS Safari and Android Chrome paint over a tapped element is the loudest 'this is a website' signal and fights the designed press feedback; removing it removes the only feedback the browser gave, so :active has to replace it.
  - Sources: eks-skills-mobile-native-skill, eks-readme.
- **Press feedback scales to 0.97, briefly.** Scale every pressable element to 0.97 while it is pressed (:active on the web; keep it within 0.95–0.98), scaling the whole element so its label and icons come along, with a transform transition of 100–160ms ease-out on the web and 100–150ms in React Native (Pressable plus a Reanimated CSS transition, with 120ms and a 3% scale as the ceiling), using the codebase's existing ease-out curve rather than a new one. Values: press-scale `0.97`; web-duration `100–160ms`; react-native-duration `100–150ms`; easing `ease-out (var(--ease-out); don't fork a new curve)`; web-sample `transition: transform 100ms var(--ease-out), background 100ms; .button:active { transform: scale(0.97); background: var(--gray-4); }`; react-native-recipe `transitionProperty: 'transform', transitionDuration: '120ms', transitionTimingFunction: 'cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)', pressed: transform [{ scale: 0.97 }]`; ceiling `120ms and a 3% scale for something touched this often`; subtle-range `0.95–0.98 (improve-animations audit: keep it subtle)`. (STD-mobile-touch-05)
  - Sets: `motion.scale.press` 0.97, `motion.duration.micro` 100ms (STD-easing-duration-07 wins).
  - Why: Scale takes the label and icons with it, so the press reads as physical and confirms the interface heard the user; the React Native recipe treats 120ms and a 3% scale as the ceiling for something touched this often.
  - Sources: eks-skills-mobile-native-skill, eks-skills-animate-expo-skill, eks-skills-animate-expo-recipes, eks-skills-apple-design-skill, eks-skills-animate-recipes, eks-skills-emil-design-eng-skill, eks-skills-review-animations-standards, eks-skills-improve-animations-audit, eks-skills-find-animation-opportunities-skill, ek-7-practical-animation-tips, ek-agents-with-taste, ek-you-dont-need-animations, ek-building-an-animation-course, eks-skills-animate-skill.
- **Remove the tap delay on tappables.** Apply touch-action: manipulation to button, a, [role="button"] and every other tappable element. Values: declaration `touch-action: manipulation`; selectors `button, a, [role="button"], .tappable`; delay-removed `300ms`. (STD-mobile-touch-06)
  - Why: Browsers wait after a tap (the 300ms click delay) to see whether a double-tap zoom follows, and iOS Safari still delays on some elements even with width=device-width; manipulation says the element never double-tap-zooms, so click fires immediately.
  - Sources: eks-skills-mobile-native-skill, eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Add double-tap handling only where needed.** Add double-tap detection only where a double-tap action truly exists. (STD-mobile-touch-07, should)
  - Why: Double-tap detection unavoidably delays single taps, so only pay that cost where a double-tap does something.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Let a drifting finger keep its press.** Keep a press alive when the finger drifts a little (pressRetentionOffset in React Native, about 10px of hysteresis or hit padding on the web), and let the user cancel a tap by dragging away and back. Values: react-native `pressRetentionOffset (the recipe sets pressRetentionOffset={16})`; web `~10px of hysteresis/hit padding around the target`. (STD-mobile-touch-08, should)
  - Why: A finger drifting a few pixels should not cancel a press the user meant.
  - Sources: eks-skills-animate-expo-skill, eks-skills-animate-expo-recipes, eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Touch targets 44pt on iOS, 48dp on Android.** Make every touch target at least 44×44pt on iOS and 48dp on Android, and give small controls on the web a 44px hit area for touch; when the visual is smaller, grow the hit area (hitSlop, or a pseudo-element on the web), never the visual. Values: ios `44×44pt`; android `48dp`; web `44px minimum hit area for touch (pseudo-element)`; react-native `hitSlop (the recipe sets hitSlop={12})`. (STD-mobile-touch-09)
  - Sets: `size.target.touch` 44px, `size.target.min` 44px.
  - Why: Small buttons are hard to tap; hitSlop brings a small icon up to the 44pt target without growing it.
  - Sources: eks-skills-animate-expo-skill, eks-skills-animate-expo-recipes, ek-agents-with-taste, eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Size full-height layouts with dvh and svh.** Use height: 100dvh for app shells, drawers and bottom-pinned UI and min-height: 100svh for marketing heroes and first screens; never use 100vh or lvh for them (keep a 100vh line above only as a fallback when the support matrix needs old browsers). Values: app-shell `height: 100dvh`; hero `min-height: 100svh`; avoid `100vh, lvh`. (STD-mobile-touch-10)
  - Why: 100vh is the largest viewport, so on load it overflows by the URL bar and a bottom-pinned button sits under it; dvh tracks the visible area as the browser chrome shows and hides, while svh is stable and never cut off, and dvh on a marketing hero causes layout shifts mid-scroll.
  - Sources: eks-skills-mobile-native-skill, eks-readme.
- **Form inputs at 16px or larger.** Set the text of input, textarea and select to at least 16px (1rem at the default root size); if the design wants smaller input text on desktop, apply the 16px only under @media (pointer: coarse). Values: input-font-size `16px`; coarse-only-variant `@media (pointer: coarse) { input, textarea, select { font-size: 16px; } }`. (STD-mobile-touch-11)
  - Sets: `font.size.input` 16px.
  - Why: iOS Safari zooms the page when focus lands on an input under 16px and does not zoom back out on blur, leaving the user on a cropped, drifted layout.
  - Sources: eks-skills-mobile-native-skill, eks-readme.
- **Open the right software keyboard per field.** Give each field the keyboard it needs: inputmode="numeric" for codes, inputmode="decimal" for amounts, type="email" and type="tel" for those fields, autocapitalize="none" and autocorrect="off" on usernames and codes, and an enterkeyhint ("send", "search" or "done") so the return key says what it does. Values: codes `inputmode="numeric"`; amounts `inputmode="decimal"`; email `type="email"`; phone `type="tel"`; usernames-and-codes `autocapitalize="none" autocorrect="off"`; return-key `enterkeyhint="send" / "search" / "done"`. (STD-mobile-touch-13, should)
  - Why: A field should open the software keyboard its content needs, and enterkeyhint makes the return key say what it does; the source sets these while fixing inputs for a phone.
  - Sources: eks-skills-mobile-native-skill.
- **Contain overscroll in app layouts.** In apps with their own scroll containers, a drawer the user drags down, or a canvas, set overscroll-behavior: none on html and body and overflow-y: auto with overscroll-behavior: contain on every inner scrollable; keep the page's default overscroll only for a scrolling document where pull-to-refresh is welcome. Values: root `html, body { overscroll-behavior: none; }`; inner-scrollables `overflow-y: auto; overscroll-behavior: contain;`; scrolling-document `drop overscroll-behavior: none from html`. (STD-mobile-touch-14)
  - Why: Scrolling past the top triggers pull-to-refresh on Android Chrome and the whole-page rubber band on iOS, which is wrong in an app; contain keeps a container's own native-feeling bounce but stops scroll from chaining to the page behind it.
  - Sources: eks-skills-mobile-native-skill.
- **Never stop overscroll with touchmove listeners.** Never stop overscroll or pull-to-refresh with a touchmove listener that calls preventDefault(); use overscroll-behavior instead. Values: never `touchmove + preventDefault()`; instead `overscroll-behavior`. (STD-mobile-touch-15)
  - Why: The listener blocks scrolling entirely and makes the listener non-passive, which costs frames.
  - Sources: eks-skills-mobile-native-skill.
- **Paint edge to edge, pad the safe areas.** Add viewport-fit=cover to the viewport meta tag and pad fixed headers, bottom tab bars, toasts and sheets with env(safe-area-inset-*), with a 0px fallback when the inset is used in calc(); in React Native, offset floating UI such as toasts by the safe-area insets. Values: viewport-meta `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover" />`; header `padding-top: env(safe-area-inset-top)`; bottom-bar `padding-bottom: env(safe-area-inset-bottom)`; sheet `padding-bottom: calc(1rem + env(safe-area-inset-bottom))`; calc-fallback `env(safe-area-inset-bottom, 0px)`; react-native-toast `bottom: insets.bottom + 16, left: 16, right: 16`. (STD-mobile-touch-16)
  - Why: Native apps paint edge to edge and pad their content away from the notch, Dynamic Island and home indicator; without viewport-fit=cover every env() inset is 0px, and a toast at bottom: 16 sits under the home indicator on every modern iPhone.
  - Sources: eks-skills-mobile-native-skill, eks-skills-animate-expo-recipes, eks-readme.
- **Make controls unselectable, keep content selectable.** Set user-select: none, -webkit-user-select: none and -webkit-touch-callout: none on controls (button, [role="button"], tabs, chips, drag handles) and never on body or on text that is content. Values: controls `user-select: none; -webkit-user-select: none; -webkit-touch-callout: none;`; selectors `button, [role="button"], .tab, .chip, .drag-handle`; never `user-select: none on body`. (STD-mobile-touch-17)
  - Why: Holding a finger on a web button selects its label or pops the copy/share callout, which native controls never do, while users copy addresses, error messages and order numbers from content; the same declaration is correct on a button and a defect on body text.
  - Sources: eks-skills-mobile-native-skill.
- **Set touch-action per gesture surface.** On custom gesture surfaces set touch-action to what the browser may still do: pan-y on a horizontal JavaScript carousel, pan-x on a vertical sheet handle, and none only on a surface whose gesture owns every axis (a drag-to-dismiss sheet, a slider), never on something the user must scroll past. Values: horizontal-carousel `touch-action: pan-y`; vertical-sheet-handle `touch-action: pan-x`; owns-every-axis `touch-action: none`. (STD-mobile-touch-18)
  - Why: A horizontal swipe is ambiguous to the browser, which often jitters the page up while the carousel moves; none means the element handles everything, so elsewhere the user cannot scroll past it.
  - Sources: eks-skills-mobile-native-skill.
- **Prefer native scroll-snap carousels.** When a carousel can be native scroll, build it with scroll-snap-type: x mandatory on the track and scroll-snap-align: start on the slides instead of a JavaScript gesture. Values: track `scroll-snap-type: x mandatory`; slide `scroll-snap-align: start`. (STD-mobile-touch-19, should)
  - Why: The browser's own physics beat a hand-rolled spring, and touch-action becomes unnecessary.
  - Sources: eks-skills-mobile-native-skill.
- **One theme-color per color scheme.** Ship one theme-color meta tag per prefers-color-scheme plus <meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark">, valued at the color at the very top of the page (the header background, not the brand color); update it from JavaScript when the theme switches by class, and make an installed PWA's status-bar style and manifest colors the same decision. Values: light `<meta name="theme-color" media="(prefers-color-scheme: light)" content="<header background>" />`; dark `<meta name="theme-color" media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" content="<header background>" />`; color-scheme `<meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark" />`; sample-values `#ffffff (light), #0a0a0a (dark)`; nextjs `viewport export themeColor: [{ media, color }]`; pwa `apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style, manifest theme_color and background_color`. (STD-mobile-touch-20)
  - Why: The status bar and browser chrome take their color from theme-color, so a single value gives light mode a dark bar or dark mode a white one.
  - Sources: eks-skills-mobile-native-skill.
- **Ship the mobile baseline first.** Before the first component of a mobile-facing web app, ship the baseline: the viewport meta with width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover and interactive-widget=resizes-content; one theme-color per scheme; html with -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent, -webkit-text-size-adjust: 100% and overscroll-behavior: none; 16px inputs; touch-action: manipulation and user-select: none on button, a and [role="button"]; and every :hover rule inside @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine). Values: viewport-meta `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1, viewport-fit=cover, interactive-widget=resizes-content" />`; html `-webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent; -webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%; overscroll-behavior: none;`; inputs `input, textarea, select { font-size: 16px; }`; controls `button, a, [role="button"] { touch-action: manipulation; user-select: none; -webkit-user-select: none; }`; hover `@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) { /* all :hover rules */ }`. (STD-mobile-touch-21)
  - Why: It is the floor for feeling native on mobile; interactive-widget=resizes-content makes the software keyboard shrink the layout viewport on Android Chrome so 100dvh and bottom-pinned inputs react as they do on iOS, and -webkit-text-size-adjust: 100% prevents font inflation in landscape.
  - Sources: eks-skills-mobile-native-skill.
- **Report mobile fixes in a few lines.** After mobile work, report in a few lines what was wrong (the symptom and a one-line why), what changed (file and declaration) and what still needs a phone or an on-device feel check, without padding it into a report. (STD-mobile-touch-24, should)
  - Why: The code is the deliverable, and gestures, velocity handoff and haptic timing cannot be judged from code.
  - Sources: eks-skills-mobile-native-skill, eks-skills-animate-expo-skill.
- **Ignore extra fingers during a drag.** Once a drag starts, ignore every additional touch point until the user releases (for example, return early from the press handler while isDragging is true). Values: guard `if (isDragging) return`. (STD-mobile-touch-28)
  - Why: Otherwise adding or switching a finger mid-drag makes the element jump to the new position, and the drawer feels off.
  - Sources: ek-building-a-drawer-component, eks-skills-animate-recipes, eks-skills-review-animations-standards, eks-skills-emil-design-eng-skill.
- **Apply each mobile fix where its reason applies.** Ship every mobile fix with its reason and apply it only where that reason applies, not globally out of habit: user-select: none belongs on a button, never on body text. Values: example `user-select: none on controls only, never on body`. (STD-mobile-touch-70)
  - Why: Each fix has a why, and the same declaration is correct in one place and a defect in another; user-select: none on body text is a defect, on a button it is correct.
  - Sources: eks-skills-mobile-native-skill.

**Visual details**
- **Cap body text near 65ch.** Cap the width of body text at about 65ch instead of letting it stretch the full width of its container. Values: body-measure `65ch`. (STD-visual-details-01)
  - Why: Line length stays comfortable to read.
  - Sources: ek-agents-with-taste.
- **Tabular digits for changing numbers.** Apply font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums to price columns and to numbers that change in place, such as tickers, timers and counters. Values: font-variant-numeric `tabular-nums`. (STD-visual-details-02)
  - Why: Fixed-width digits line up so a price column reads cleanly, and changing numbers do not shift around as they update.
  - Sources: ek-agents-with-taste, eks-skills-animation-vocabulary-skill.
- **Use the ellipsis character.** Write the single ellipsis character (…) in markup and UI strings, never three periods (...). Values: use `…`; avoid `...`. (STD-visual-details-03)
  - Why: Truncation then follows the container instead of snapping at a fixed character count.
  - Sources: ek-agents-with-taste.
- **Loosen tracking on uppercase labels.** Give uppercase labels looser letter-spacing than the same text in sentence case. (STD-visual-details-04)
  - Why: Tight uppercase reads cramped.
  - Sources: ek-agents-with-taste.
- **Make letter-spacing specific to size.** Never use one letter-spacing value for every size: tighten large display text and headings (for example letter-spacing: -0.02em), give small text slightly positive tracking, and leave body text near 0. Values: display-letter-spacing (example) `-0.02em`; body-letter-spacing `near 0`. (STD-visual-details-05)
  - Why: Letters read too far apart as text grows, and small text needs slightly positive tracking for legibility, so a fixed letter-spacing is wrong somewhere.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Leading tracks size inversely.** Set line-height inversely to size: tight on large headings (for example 1.05 for display text), looser on body copy (for example 1.5), higher for scripts with tall ascenders and descenders, and tighter for dense, information-heavy UI. Values: display-line-height (example) `1.05`; body-line-height (example) `1.5`. (STD-visual-details-06, should)
  - Why: Type should change shape with size, as Apple designs it; the source gives no further reason for the example values.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Build hierarchy from weight, size, leading.** Build type hierarchy from weight, size and line-height set together, not from font size alone. (STD-visual-details-07, should)
  - Why: The source states the set as the rule and adds that weight gives presence without taking more space.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Emphasise with weight, not italic.** Emphasise interface text with weight (bold); keep italic for citations and linguistic stress in prose. (STD-visual-details-08, should)
  - Why: Italic hierarchy reads like print editorial, not UI hierarchy, while weight adds presence without taking more space.
  - Sources: ek-agents-with-taste, eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Reserve underlines for links.** Underline only links; emphasise non-link text with weight or color, never with an underline. (STD-visual-details-09)
  - Why: Underline stays a reliable affordance, and people are not tempted to click inert copy.
  - Sources: ek-agents-with-taste.
- **Metric-matched fallback font stack.** Declare a fallback font stack whose x-height and weight match the primary typeface. (STD-visual-details-10)
  - Why: Font loading then does not cause layout shift.
  - Sources: ek-agents-with-taste.
- **Default to the system font.** Start from the platform's system font and switch to a custom typeface only for a stated reason. Values: root-font (example) `font: 100%/1.5 system-ui, sans-serif`. (STD-visual-details-11, should)
  - Why: The system font already ships optical sizing, tracking tables and legibility tuning.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Legible text on translucent surfaces.** Over blurred or translucent surfaces, avoid flat gray text: use higher-contrast text, a slightly heavier weight and a small letter-spacing increase. (STD-visual-details-13, should)
  - Why: Vibrancy keeps text legible over changing backgrounds.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Semi-transparent shadow over solid border.** Separate surfaces with a semi-transparent shadow rather than a solid, opaque border. (STD-visual-details-14, should)
  - Why: A solid border where a semi-transparent shadow belongs is one of the small agent mistakes that compound into an interface that is not great.
  - Sources: eks-readme.
- **Scroll-edge effects, not hard dividers.** Instead of a 1px border under a sticky header, fade a small blur or gradient mask where content meets floating chrome, and only where floating UI actually overlaps content. Values: avoid `1px border under a sticky header`. (STD-visual-details-15, should)
  - Why: The source prefers a soft edge that appears only where floating chrome overlaps content over a permanent hard divider; it gives no further reason.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Translucent bars and sheets.** Build navigation bars, toolbars and sheets as translucent layers (backdrop-filter: blur() over a semi-transparent background) with content scrolling underneath, not as opaque bars that take a fixed strip. Values: toolbar-background (example) `rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.6)`; toolbar-backdrop-filter (example) `blur(20px) saturate(180%)`; toolbar-top-edge (example) `1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.4)`. (STD-visual-details-16, should)
  - Why: Translucent materials bring structure as a floating functional layer without stealing focus.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Material weight encodes hierarchy.** Use darker, heavier materials to separate structural regions such as sidebars, and lighter materials to draw attention to interactive elements such as buttons. (STD-visual-details-17, should)
  - Why: Material weight encodes hierarchy.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Never stack light translucent surfaces.** Never place a light translucent surface on top of another light translucent surface. (STD-visual-details-18)
  - Why: Legibility collapses when light translucent layers stack.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Bigger surfaces read thicker.** Give bigger surfaces a stronger blur and a deeper shadow than small chips. (STD-visual-details-19, should)
  - Why: Bigger surfaces should read as thicker material.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Scrim for modal tasks only.** Pair a modal task's surface with a dimming scrim and push the background back or down; give a parallel, non-blocking panel translucency and offset without a scrim; in a stack of sheets, progressively dim and push back each parent layer. (STD-visual-details-20, should)
  - Why: Dimming focuses a modal task, while separating without a scrim keeps a parallel flow unbroken.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Color on solid layers.** Put color on a solid layer, not on a translucent foreground surface. (STD-visual-details-21, should)
  - Why: The source puts it with vibrancy, which keeps text legible over changing backgrounds; it gives no separate reason.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Colors adapt to light and dark.** Make interface colors adapt to light and dark mode: give each color role a light value and a dark value. (STD-visual-details-24, should)
  - Why: The source lists colors that adapt to light and dark as part of the craft that builds trust.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Restrained look with no project.** When prototyping with no project to draw tokens from (an empty directory, or the person is just exploring), use a restrained default look: neutral grays, one accent color and the system font stack. Values: grays `neutral`; accents `one`; font `system font stack`. (STD-visual-details-25)
  - Why: The source gives no reason; with no project there are no tokens for the variants to use [inferred].
  - Sources: eks-skills-prototype-skill.
- **Use and extend existing tokens.** Build UI from the project's existing tokens (colors, radii, spacing, fonts, easing and duration variables) and extend them when something is missing; never add a parallel set, and never hand-type or approximate a value such as cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1). (STD-visual-details-26)
  - Why: Every variant should look like it could ship in the product tomorrow, and a parallel token system is a defect.
  - Sources: eks-skills-prototype-skill, eks-skills-animate-skill, eks-skills-find-animation-opportunities-skill, eks-skills-improve-animations-skill, eks-skills-improve-animations-audit, eks-skills-animate-expo-skill, eks-skills-review-animations-skill, eks-skills-mobile-native-skill.
- **Make every value a deliberate choice.** Make every spacing, timing and alignment value a deliberate choice you can defend. (STD-visual-details-27, should)
  - Why: Uncompromising attention to detail builds trust.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **No jitter, misalignment or rotation breaks.** Do not ship jittery scrolling, misaligned icons or layouts that break when the device rotates. (STD-visual-details-28)
  - Why: These read as carelessness.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Hierarchy makes the key thing obvious.** Use order, spacing and contrast so the most important thing on a screen is the most obvious. (STD-visual-details-29, should)
  - Why: Clarity through hierarchy is part of simplicity.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Aim for simplicity, not minimalism.** Strip what is unnecessary so the core purpose shows, make every element earn its place, and add context where it simplifies; do not bury everything in one place to look minimal. (STD-visual-details-30, should)
  - Why: Burying everything in one place looks minimal but is not simple; sometimes adding context simplifies (a video scrubber that shows time remaining).
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Show the common path first.** Show the common path first and put advanced options one level deeper. (STD-visual-details-31, should)
  - Why: The source lists this under simplicity.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Controls sit near what they change.** Place each control near what it affects and arrange controls to mirror what they change. (STD-visual-details-32, should)
  - Why: Proximity implies relationship; if a control needs a label to explain it, the mapping is weak.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Every screen answers wayfinding.** Never trap the user: every screen should answer Where am I? Where can I go? What's there? How do I get out? (STD-visual-details-33)
  - Why: The source lists wayfinding as a tactical rule serving the design principles.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Name navigation items for their contents.** Name navigation items for their contents (for example "Progress", "Library"), not with vague umbrellas such as "Home". Values: good (examples) `Progress, Library`; avoid (example) `Home`. (STD-visual-details-34, should)
  - Why: Specificity creates predictability.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Keep interface copy plain and concise.** Keep interface copy concise: plain language, no jargon and fewer steps. (STD-visual-details-35, should)
  - Why: The source lists conciseness under simplicity.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Same look, same behaviour.** Make things that look the same behave the same and live in the same place. (STD-visual-details-36)
  - Why: People can then predict what happens next (close is always top-left on macOS).
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Break familiar patterns only with proof.** Break a familiar pattern only when you can prove the new one is better, and test it rather than assume. (STD-visual-details-37, should)
  - Why: Familiarity lets people build on what they already know.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Metaphors with honest physics.** Use metaphors that are neither too literal nor too abstract (a trash can means delete) and honour their physics. (STD-visual-details-38, should)
  - Why: The source lists this under familiarity: building on what people already know.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Offer choices, not one forced path.** Keep people in control by offering choices instead of forcing a single path. (STD-visual-details-39, should)
  - Why: The source names this agency.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Undo for slips, confirm only destruction.** Give easy undo for slips, and use a confirmation dialog only for genuinely destructive, irreversible actions, sparingly. (STD-visual-details-40)
  - Why: Overusing confirmation dialogs trains people to click through them.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Ask for private data carefully.** Ask for private data at the moment it is needed, only for what is needed, and say why. (STD-visual-details-41, should)
  - Why: The source names this responsibility: acting in the user's interest.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Adapt to platform and situation.** Adapt the design to the platform and situation: quick touch interactions on a phone, deep workflows with precise pointer control on desktop. (STD-visual-details-42, should)
  - Why: The source names this flexibility: designing for different contexts and devices.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Design for every age and ability.** Design for the full range of age, language, expertise and ability. (STD-visual-details-43, should)
  - Why: The source names this flexibility: designing for the full range of abilities.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Decide what not to build.** Decide what not to build, and spend the user's time, attention and trust only on features that pay off. (STD-visual-details-44, should)
  - Why: Every feature asks for the user's time, attention and trust.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Anticipate misuse and harm.** Anticipate misuse and harm, especially in AI features: add previews, confirmations and disclaimers, and cut a feature whose risk outweighs its value. (STD-visual-details-45, should)
  - Why: The source names this responsibility: acting in the user's interest (an allergy-aware recipe app must not suggest a harmful ingredient).
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Keep evolving the design.** Keep evolving the design as features and hardware change. (STD-visual-details-46, should)
  - Why: Craft needs iteration and longevity.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Decide the emotion, then reinforce it.** Decide the emotion people should feel (for example calm, confident or excited) and reinforce it in every decision instead of tacking delight on top. Values: emotions (examples) `calm, confident, excited`. (STD-visual-details-47, should)
  - Why: Delight is the result of getting the other seven principles right, not confetti tacked on top.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Reason with the eight principles.** Name Apple's eight principles (purpose, agency, responsibility, familiarity, flexibility, simplicity, craft, delight) when making and defending design decisions. Values: principles `purpose, agency, responsibility, familiarity, flexibility, simplicity, craft, delight`. (STD-visual-details-48, should)
  - Why: The source says to use them as the names you reason with.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Feedback on every action.** Give feedback as soon as possible: confirm meaningful actions (a loading state while a submitted form works, a success state after copy to clipboard), expose ongoing status, warn before problems, and validate form input inline rather than on submit. Values: feedback-kinds `status, completion, warning, error`. (STD-visual-details-49)
  - Why: The interface should feel as if it is listening to the user.
  - Sources: ek-7-practical-animation-tips, eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Polish the unseen details.** Build the small details users will not consciously notice, such as matching the behaviour people expect from native components. (STD-visual-details-50, should)
  - Why: In the aggregate, unseen details become visible and compound; when a feature works exactly as someone assumes, they carry on without a second thought.
  - Sources: ek-building-a-toast-component, ek-building-a-drawer-component, ek-7-practical-animation-tips, ek-the-magic-of-clip-path, eks-skills-emil-design-eng-skill.
- **Excellent defaults before options.** Make the default easing, timing and visual design of a component excellent before adding options. (STD-visual-details-51, should)
  - Why: Most users never customize, so a component should ship beautiful out of the box.
  - Sources: eks-skills-emil-design-eng-skill.
- **Pick libraries from the curated list.** When a frontend task needs a library, identify the task rather than the library the person named, and recommend one library from the curated list in one sentence, not a menu of options when the list has a clear answer; do not substitute an alternative from outside the list unless the person asks for one, say explicitly when a task is not covered before recommending from general knowledge, and never install an abandoned package. Values: unstyled accessible UI (dialogs, popovers, menus, selects) `base-ui`; command menus (⌘K) `cmdk`; toasts `Sonner`; OTP / verification code inputs `input-otp`; GUIs / control panels `Leva (dialkit alternative)`; general animation (springs, layout, enter/exit) `motion`; animating numbers `NumberFlow`; animated text `torph`; 3D globes `Cobe`; dynamic OG images `Satori`; syntax highlighting `shiki`; real-time / streaming charts `Liveline`; other charts `recharts`; drag and drop `dnd kit`; virtualization `Virtuoso`; state management `zustand`; conditional className `clsx`; variant styling for Tailwind `cva`; theme switching / dark mode `next-themes`. (STD-visual-details-55)
  - Why: The picks are deliberate and taste-driven; the list exists so an agent picks the right library instead of hand-rolling a component or installing an abandoned package.
  - Sources: eks-skills-pick-ui-library-skill, eks-readme.
- **Reuse installed libraries first.** Read package.json before recommending a library: use a listed library the project already has, and when it uses a competitor (for example react-window instead of Virtuoso), flag the recommendation without replacing the dependency unless asked. Values: check `package.json`. (STD-visual-details-56)
  - Why: The source says not to churn a working dependency without being asked; it gives no further reason.
  - Sources: eks-skills-pick-ui-library-skill.
- **Never hand-roll standard components.** When a task needs a component rather than an animation (a toast, a drawer, a command menu, a dropdown), pick a library instead of hand-rolling it; build toasts with Sonner, never by hand or with a modal library. Values: toasts `Sonner`; command menus `cmdk`; dropdowns `base-ui`; install `npm install sonner`. (STD-visual-details-57)
  - Why: Hand-rolling these is how you end up with a <div> dropdown and no focus management; for toasts, Sonner exists for exactly this.
  - Sources: eks-skills-animate-skill, eks-skills-pick-ui-library-skill, eks-readme, sonner-home.
- **Animate numbers with NumberFlow.** When a number animates (a counter, price or stat), use NumberFlow instead of animating it by re-rendering the text. Values: library `NumberFlow`. (STD-visual-details-59)
  - Why: NumberFlow handles digit transitions properly.
  - Sources: eks-skills-pick-ui-library-skill.
- **Shared state in zustand.** Keep shared state in zustand instead of a useState-per-component web of props. Values: library `zustand`. (STD-visual-details-61)
  - Why: The source lists a useState-per-component web of props for shared state as a mismatch.
  - Sources: eks-skills-pick-ui-library-skill.
- **clsx or cva for conditional classes.** Build conditional className strings with clsx, or with cva when the component has real variants (size, intent, state); never nest template-literal ternaries three conditions deep. Values: ad-hoc `clsx`; variants `cva`; limit `three conditions deep`. (STD-visual-details-62)
  - Why: clsx is for ad-hoc conditional classes and cva for variants that deserve a typed API; they compose.
  - Sources: eks-skills-pick-ui-library-skill.
- **Let people personalise when one layout can't fit.** When no single layout fits everyone, let people personalise it: rearrange controls and hide what they don't use. (STD-visual-details-64, should)
  - Why: The source lists this under flexibility: designing for different contexts, devices and the full range of abilities.
  - Sources: eks-skills-apple-design-skill.
- **Known meanings keep their colours.** Keep the commonly known colour for a meaning, unless the person asks otherwise: approved or success green, rejected or error red, pending or warning amber, info blue; a well-known app or channel keeps its own colour (Microsoft Teams purple, email in Outlook blue, a call green). The brand accent never takes a meaning that has a known colour. Values: success `green`; danger `red`; warning `amber`; info `blue`. (STD-visual-details-65)
  - Why: People recognise the known colours at a glance, and a product that uses them feels made with care, not by AI.
  - Sources: owner-house-rules.
